details.label: Discussion
details.text: A multicellular cluster continues to propagate southward, with a history of producing measured hail over 1 inch in diameter, with MRMS MESH indicating up to 2 inch diameter hail potentially falling. As these storms continue to propagate farther south, they will encounter an even drier/deeper boundary layer, which may foster enough evaporative cooling to generate a few severe gusts via dry microbursts. It is unclear how far south storms will progress given increasingly weaker downstream deep-layer shear and overall drier air. Convective trends will continue to be monitored for the need of a Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Easterly upslope flow across western NE/KS into eastern Colorado to the foothills is contributing to steadily increasing moisture into eastern Colorado/southeastern Wyoming. Recent ACARS soundings from DEN show MLCIN remains. MLCAPE around 1000-2000 J/kg is noted within SPC Mesoanalysis from eastern Colorado into western Nebraska/northern Kansas. Convection has increased along the high terrain. Guidance suggests that with further heating and forcing for ascent with an upstream disturbance shifting eastward late this afternoon/early evening, thunderstorms will increase in coverage spread into the lower plains in eastern Colorado and eventually into portions of the central Plains. With modest westerly flow aloft and deep layer shear around 30-35 kts, supercell modes will be favored initially. Large hail and severe gusts will be the primary threat, given steep low to mid-level lapse rates and aforementioned thermodynamic environment.
